source: Brutally Honest LinkedIn Advice From Alex Hormozi (applied to cold DMs)

sell_result_not_vehicle.name: Sell the Result, Not the Vehicle
sell_result_not_vehicle.when: When writing LinkedIn DMs, ad copy, or any marketing message
sell_result_not_vehicle.essence: Do not advertise what you do or how you do it. Advertise the result the prospect wants. The vehicle is just how you get them there.
sell_result_not_vehicle.example: Instead of 'we do LinkedIn outreach for B2B companies' say 'we help you book 10+ calls a week from LinkedIn.'
sell_result_not_vehicle.how_to_test: Run small tests comparing headlines that state the result vs headlines that describe the service. The result-based version will attract more and better leads.

segment_before_write.name: Segment Before You Write
segment_before_write.when: When planning LinkedIn outreach or any cold campaign
segment_before_write.essence: Figure out who before you worry about the words. The right message to the right person beats a perfect message to the wrong one every time.
segment_before_write.data: HubSpot saw 791% increase in ROI from segmentation alone. Not from writing better emails. From sending the right thing to the right person.
segment_before_write.application: Build two narrow lists of slightly different people. Send them the same message. Let replies tell you which one actually cares. Then double down.

lead_magnet_complete_solution.name: Lead Magnet = Complete Solution to a Narrow Problem
lead_magnet_complete_solution.when: When designing the first DM or any cold outreach offer
lead_magnet_complete_solution.essence: A lead magnet is a complete solution to a narrow problem. Both halves matter: it fully solves something AND that something is small and specific.
lead_magnet_complete_solution.common_mistake: A pitch deck is not a lead magnet. A case study about how amazing your company is is also not a lead magnet. If it does not help them on its own it is just a pitch in a costume.
lead_magnet_complete_solution.application_on_linkedin: First message should feel like a gift. No calendar link. No pitch. Offer something valuable for free. Solve one small problem. Ask for nothing. The sale comes later after they have gotten value.

multi_touch_follow_up.name: Multi-Touch LinkedIn Follow-Up Sequence
multi_touch_follow_up.when: When creating a follow-up sequence for LinkedIn DMs
multi_touch_follow_up.essence: The acquisition cost is the connection request. You already paid to get their attention. Do not throw that investment away by sending one message and moving on.
multi_touch_follow_up.cadence: 3 touches per week is fine if quality is high. Every message should give a new reason to reply. Do not just bump.
sequence: Day 0: Personalized message + voice note (voice notes have highest open rate because almost nobody sends them)
Day 3: Send a resource (article, breakdown, template that helps them)
multi_touch_follow_up.note: On LinkedIn 3 DMs a week to a stranger can feel desperate. Use multiple touches spread out with value each time. Voice notes work best because they are rare and personal.

volume_is_bridge.name: Volume is the Bridge to the First Dollar
volume_is_bridge.when: When someone is not getting results from outreach or feels like they are failing
volume_is_bridge.essence: The first dollar is always the hardest because you have to learn many little skills before the big payoff. Every message or call is a brick in the bridge. Keep laying bricks and eventually it becomes unreasonable for you to fail.
volume_is_bridge.the_rule: Do another 5000. If you are not getting results you have not done enough volume yet. It is unreasonable to suck forever if you keep going.
volume_is_bridge.warning: Volume only works on top of the other rules. Without knowing who to target, what to offer, and how to follow up, volume is just spamming with extra steps.

key_tactics: Market the outcome, not the process. Nobody buys the vehicle. They buy the destination.
791% ROI gain comes from segmentation, not better writing. Send right things to right people.
First DM is a gift with no ask. Free sample at the supermarket principle.
Voice notes on LinkedIn have highest engagement because almost nobody uses them.
Every follow-up message needs a new reason to reply. Never just 'bumping this.'
The acquisition cost is already paid. Following up protects that investment.
Volume is necessary but not sufficient. Pair it with targeting, offer design, and multi-touch sequences.
Use AI to personalize at scale (analyze profile, generate custom hooks per person).
